items.title: Networking and Concurrency for iOS Apps
items.description:
In this course, you'll learn how to integrate data from the Internet and websites into your applications, including APIs, networking, authentication, and concurrency. You'll also learn how to integrate these concepts into iOS app UI design, with a focus on practical application through a travel journey project. By the end of the course, you'll have a solid foundation in skills for leveraging networking and managing concurrency in your iOS apps.APIs and Networking for iOS Developers
Explore APIs and networking in iOS, including making HTTP requests, handling responses/errors, and sending/receiving data using URLSession and Codable.
 Authentication for iOS Apps
Explore implementing Sign In with Apple: learn setup, manage authentication states and data, alongside traditional username/password methods.
 Concurrency in iOS Apps
Explore iOS concurrency: from responsive UIs and Swift's async/await, actors, to structured concurrency for efficient, error-handled asynchronous coding.
 Integrating Concurrency and Network into iOS App UI
Enhance iOS apps with concurrency for smoother network UIs, covering async/await, error handling, offline modes, and UI feedback on network status.

items.title: Certificate in Foundation Studies
items.description:
The Certificate in Foundation Studies in Tourism Studies will provide students with the knowledge as well as the personal and inter-personal skills and organisational framework upon which to build their future undergraduate Tourism studies.     The primary aim of the course is to provide students enrolled in this course with the knowledge base,  transferable skills,  communicative skills,  and general competence to allow them to progress successfully onto the University of Malta’s undergraduate Tourism Studies course. The course offers specific training in those core Tourism and Academic English areas where these students require further assistance and development.     The course will provide teaching in the subject areas of history,  cultural heritage,  tourism,  hospitality,  psychology,  communications,  economics,  accounting,  business mathematics,  statistics,  basic research skills,  reasoning,  as well as academic English skills. In addition,  students will be expected to attend regular tutorial sessions for all study-units. During the tutorial sessions students will be expected to show adequate revision of the week’s work. At the same time,  tutorials are intended as scheduled directed learning sessions during which students will be able to apply theoretical and conceptual frameworks as well as practice verbal and written expressions.     This course will include continuous assessment to build up a realistic profile of the student’s core abilities and competencies. Tutors will be required to assess students periodically. As the course progresses and the language and subject contents improve,  students will be expected to show evidence of higher-level analytical and evaluation skills.      Skills such as the student’s ability to apply their knowledge base and to show evidence of self-directed learning during tutorials will be assessed in the first and second semesters.     Student performance will be monitored continuously by the area coordinator and feedback will be provided through course tutors. This will allow an awareness of the student’s approach to learning and the identification of students who are encountering difficulties,  so that remedial action such as the offer of small group coaching can be provided.     Successful completion of this course will guarantee a place on the undergraduate degree programme for Tourism studies.
The course will provide students with:     � a sound knowledge of the basics of the disciplines of tourism,  hospitality,  humanities,  social sciences,  business and statistics;    � the reading,  writing,  listening,  and critical thinking skills necessary to function effectively as a Tourism student in higher education;    � training to apply scientific reasoning and analytical skills as well as training on low and high order thinking skills;     � an understanding of how to think and reason more effectively in the abstract as well as to solve problems efficiently;    � an understanding of the main features of research methods and their application.

items.title: Award in Understanding the Migrant Child's Needs
items.description:
This Award entitled ‘Understanding the Migrant Child’s Needs’ aims at equipping Community Liaison Staff participants with the necessary knowledge, skills and competences to help them increase their awareness on the migrant child’s needs. Migrant children represent a significant share of the migrant and refugee population; one in every eight migrants worldwide being a child (UNICEF, 2016). Children migrate for multiple reasons: to flee persecution, war and violence; to reunite with family members abroad; and to seek better economic and educational opportunities. Migrant children are susceptible to violence, abuse, exploitation and human trafficking. Different factors contribute to migrant children’s vulnerability, including preexisting risk factors at individual, household, community, and structural levels; the specific reasons why they have migrated; and the specific conditions they face during travel, transit, and at destination. These vulnerabilities are intensified for those migrant children who are unaccompanied or separated.
The learner will be able to: 

a)	Identify the diversity in migration tracts and reasons for migration
b)	Describe the diversity in cohorts
c)	Describe how to support living together
d)	List issues resulting from migration which may not be specifically related to education The learner will be able to:

items.title: Award in Cooperation with National, EU and International Partners
items.description:
An introduction to the main functions of Europol will be provided at the beginning of the session followed by a broad explanation of the difference between agreements which exist between supporting countries. The session will give a brief introduction to the organisation and operation centres that coordinate such support including crime categories that fall within the Europol Mandate.
Unit 4A: The European Union -Define the European Union and describe the role which it plays in diplomacy, the promotion of human rights, trade, development and humanitarian aid. Unit 4B:  Interpol - Understand the role of the organisation in the Malta Police Force and how to use its tools. Unit 4C:  Europol - Contribute towards fighting organised crime on several different fronts through an international dimension concept and an international response platform. Unit 4D:  Schengen - Delineate the main EU Institutions and their functions as well as discuss the Treaty of the Functioning of the European Union and the Treaty of Amsterdam, which includes the allocation of the areas of asylum, immigration and judicial cooperation and Police, and Judicial Co-operation in Criminal Matters. Unit 4E:  S.I.R.E.N.E  - a)	Describe the main functions of the S.I.R.E.N.E. Office; b)	Recognise the role of S.I.R.E.N.E. to support police activities; c)	Explain how S.I.R.E.N.E. can assist in relation to issued documents, vehicles, license plates, missing persons, firearms, boats and boat engines; d)	Able to refer to the S.I.R.E.N.E. manual for guidance; e)	Recognise S.I.R.E.N.E. while using the National Police System search functionality. Unit 4A: The European Union - The functions of EU institutions such as the Courts of Justice, FRA, CEPOL, Frontex, OLAF, ENISA, Eurojust, EU LISA and EASO. Unit 4B:  Interpol - Awareness about all the tools used by one of the oldest, International police Organisations, including the current databases covering amongst others: nominal data and fingerprints, firearms, travel and official documents, motor vehicles, terrorist fighters, forensics, child sexual exploitation, works of art and 100 million police records. 
Unit 4C:  Europol - A working knowledge about the Europol Agency, the types of crime that it fights, the other work that it covers, all its services and how it delivers tangible results, thanks in no small part to its cooperation with law enforcement and other agencies within and outside the EU. Unit 4D:  Schengen - A brief, historical overview regarding the steps taken along the years to make the EU what it actually is today, thus developing a sound, working knowledge about the EU Area of Freedom, Security, Justice and the Schengen area, including the compensatory measures such as the Integrated Document Security, related Schengen Visa, Passport and Residence Permit. Participants will also learn about the full impact of the Schengen Acquis on Malta. Unit 4E:  S.I.R.E.N.E  - 
A full range of knowledge about the function, tools and responsibilities of the S.I.R.E.N.E Bureau, so that Police Officers are equipped to develop competencies that would enable them to engage with the subject matter when encountered in the line of duty. Unit 4A: The European Union - Describe the functions of the European Commission, the Council of Ministers, and the European Parliament. Unit 4B:  Interpol - Carry out searches on Interpol databases in real time, using the correct and appropriate Interpol tool when and as required to contribute towards ongoing international investigations. This can be done via INTERPOL National Central Bureau, or directly at the frontline, for instance, by specialized crime units and border officials. Unit 4C:  Europol - Access all the Databases which Europol offers as just one component of its many services and support systems. Unit 4D:  Schengen -  
Engage with the subject from a law enforcement perspective by means of the material presented, including the policies and legislation that underpin Schengen and other relevant issues. The broad understanding of the operation of the Schengen Area will help develop other skills regarding the subject matter. Unit 4E:  S.I.R.E.N.E   - Help to formulate practical and theoretical responses to problems when alerted about missing persons, aliens, stolen vehicles, firearms, banknotes and stolen works of art through the sharing of data between the VIS/Mail System, the SIS/SIRENE system and the National Systems in all Member States of the Schengen Area.

items.title: Level 4  Award in Working Safely at Heights
items.description:
The objective of this Programme is for those learners already working or preparing to work in industry or in any organisation where they can be exposed to heights such as during construction work etc. Topics undertaking in this course are regarded by the Health & safety executive as being important in maintaining good practice in the safe,  prompt and effective prevention of injuries that are in most cases fatal. The Programme provides learners with the knowledge,  understanding and skills in working safely at heights
State the role and responsibilities for an individual carrying our working at heights; Describe the safe use of a personal fall arrest system; Describe the safe use of a self-retractable lanyard; Describe the safe use of mobile anchor point; Describe the safe use of mobile anchor point; Describe the safe use of a rope grab; Undertake further studies so as to gain information and knowledge on working at heights; Name the different components of personal fall equipment; Discuss with others the working procedures; Discuss the limitations and the appropriate application of travel restraint,  fall restricting and fall arrest systems; Discuss the fundamental components of travel restraint,  fall restricting and fall arrest systems; Discuss the appropriate location and use of anchor points; Discuss the importance of manufacturer’s recommendations when installing new anchor points and,  where necessary,  approval of anchor points by a professional engineer; Discuss the force required to deploy a shock absorber; Discuss the roles and responsibilities of employers,  supervisors and workers in regards to a fall rescue plan and emergency procedures; reports and maintain records of findings and actions carried out during equipment visual inspections Proceed to assess a task,  and  select the proper fall arrest equipment to use; Proceed to manage a person who is suspended on a fall arrest system following an incident; Ability to select proper anchor points; Carry out visual inspection of fall arrest equipment; Proceed to select the type of retractable lanyard needed for certain task; Proceed to select a proper fall arrest harness; Proceed to create temporally anchor points; Proceed to carry out a risk assessment and develop a rescue plan; State the steps to be taken to call for help and phone 112; Interact with other members of the work force; Use proper communication techniques when working at heights; Maintain dialogue with other members of the workforce present on site; Be able to express his opinion and discuss issues; Be able to share knowledge; Be able to list typical accidents and injuries related to working at heights in the workplace; Be able to provide instruction to others re actions to be taken in a given situation; Promote proper interaction with others so as to coordinate help during an accident; Promote proper interaction  with others so as to coordinate and prepare a work plan; Provide suitable care and maintenance information to personal fall equipment; Demonstrate competence in carrying out a proper work risk assessment; Demonstrate competence in carrying out visual inspection for fall arrest equipment; Convey proper information to other professionals,  site supervisors etc.

items.title: Award in Customer Care for Supervisory Personnel
items.description:
This training programme introduces employees already engaged in front line supervisory roles within a hotel environment to the best practices of general supervisory work, specifically in relation to employee management, customer care leadership, and client satisfaction.
At the end of this training the employee will have mastered the following skills:
a)	Demonstrate self-reflective and self-developing practices.
b)	Apply basic proactive planning practices such as planning shift briefings (pre- and post-shift) and deploying staff on duty to best cope with the expected workload arising during the shift.
